messages:
olivia (sec-eng): FYI — staging CI just flagged a SAST finding that looks like a KMS key ID in source. can someone triage?
devops-ci: [bot] pipeline #staging build 482 failed: sast: SNYK-SECRET-001 -> potential secret pattern matched
rasmus (eng): link to pipeline?
olivia (sec-eng): https://ci.redwood.example/builds/482 -> snippet in logs:
```
src/auth/kms_client.py:42 KMS_KEY = \"projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/abcd1234\"
```
rasmus (eng): hm looks like a hardcoded key identifier, not the private key itself. Could be FP if it's just a key resource name.
kevin (infra): agree, resource names can appear in config examples. but we should treat it as sensitive until confirmed. we need: reproduce, check if key exists in KMS, check recent decrypt operations (audit logs).
julia (product): if this is in an example or test fixture in repo, we should get it removed or redacted ASAP. product docs might have been copied.
carla (sre): DAST flakiness unrelated, ignore. for SAST triage: if FP then suppression with reason + link to ticket is fine. if real, rotate key and revoke.
dmitri (sec-eng): quick grep locally: `git grep abcd1234 || true` returns hits in `examples/` and `tests/fixtures/`. looks like a test fixture.
olivia (sec-eng): OK can someone open a ticket and draft suppression justification? we need RBAC check too — ensure the CI pipeline service account doesn't have KMS decrypt perms by default.
rasmus (eng): I'll open INFRASEC-1972. plan: 1) confirm key existence in project 2) check Cloud Audit Logs for `Decrypt` calls in last 30d 3) if no decrypts and in tests -> redact and add suppression 4) update pipeline SA perms.
dmitri (sec-eng): recommend adding an audit alert: log-based metric for `methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"` scoped to infra project, with pager if rate > 0 outside CI windows.
kevin (infra): for RBAC change, do not grant broad roles. give pipeline SA `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` scoped to specific keys only when needed. For example: `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:ci@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --condition='resource.name.startsWith("projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/infra/")'`
security-bot: [automated] opened ticket INFRASEC-1972 and assigned to @rasmus (eng) — link: https://jira.redwood.example/browse/INFRASEC-1972
rasmus (eng): I'll redact the fixture and push a patch to remove the resource name from tests, then request a security-review. can we do a quick non-blocking suppress on CI for this signature until PR merges?
olivia (sec-eng): +1 for temporary non-blocking suppression. we should add the exact justification in the suppression comment: `test fixture resource name, no secret material, audited no decrypts`. keep suppression for 7 days unless CI patch merged earlier.
carla (sre): note for the security review workflow: when suppression is added, require a JIRA link + reviewer annotation `sec:accepted-suppression` on the PR. automation will verify before auto-unblock.
dmitri (sec-eng): also add an entry to the SAST false-positive catalog: path, rule id, rationale, triage owner and date. helps avoid repeated churn.
julia (product): thanks — I'll check docs repo for similar fixtures.
rasmus (eng): PR: https://git.redwood.example/p/redwood/auth/+/1234 will land the redaction. adding `sec-review` label and pinging @olivia for quick sign-off.
olivia (sec-eng): got it, will review after CI passes. if anything else looks risky we'll escalate.
carla (sre): follow-up: let's also patch CI to run a lightweight audit-check step that queries KMS key metadata instead of failing on resource-name matches for `examples/` paths — reduces noise.
kevin (infra): agreed, implement a path-exclude rule in scanner config: `exclude_paths: - ^examples/ - ^tests/fixtures/` and tie suppression to repo-level policy. but be careful not to exclude `src/` accidentally.
olivia (sec-eng): summary steps added to INFRASEC-1972: reproduce -> audit logs -> redact fixtures -> temporary suppression (7d) -> update scanner exclude rules -> RBAC least-privilege for CI SA -> add audit alert. closing thread for now, will update when PR merged. :white_check_mark:
